meta.note: detail_in_practice resolves by industry key first, then falls back to 'default'.

industries.label: Education
industries.framing: K-12 districts and universities hold student data under FERPA and, increasingly, state-level AI policy. On-premises deployment keeps that data inside institutional control.

industries.label: Federal / Defense Contractors
industries.framing: Air-gapped and classified environments rule out SaaS AI outright. These are reference architectures you deploy and own, inside your own accreditation boundary.

industries.label: Financial Services
industries.framing: Regulated institutions need auditability over which model touched which data. Owning the stack makes model governance a design choice rather than a vendor disclosure.

industries.label: Food & CPG Manufacturing
industries.framing: Plant floors generate vision and sensor data continuously, and food safety documentation never stops accumulating. Both are cheaper to process where they are created.

industries.label: General Manufacturing
industries.framing: Decades of engineering documentation, live line telemetry, and simulation workloads all favor infrastructure you own over metered API calls.

industries.label: Healthcare & Life Sciences
industries.framing: PHI handling makes sending data to a hyperscaler API a compliance conversation before it is a cost conversation. On-premises inference sidesteps both.

industries.label: Legal Services
industries.framing: Privileged client material cannot go to a public API. That single constraint makes owned infrastructure the default rather than the upgrade.

industries.label: Oil & Gas
industries.framing: Remote sites with limited or intermittent connectivity cannot depend on a round trip to the cloud. Inference belongs at the edge, near the asset.

industries.label: Retail & Distribution
industries.framing: Store and DC workloads run continuously at high volume, which is exactly the profile where metered API pricing stops making sense.

industries.label: State & Local Government
industries.framing: Data sovereignty, public records obligations, and capital-friendly procurement cycles all point the same direction: own the infrastructure.

industries.label: Transportation & Logistics
industries.framing: Assets are distributed and moving. Terminal and yard-level inference beats round-tripping telemetry from every vehicle and container.

industries.label: Utilities & Energy
industries.framing: NERC CIP requirements and OT network isolation make on-premises close to mandatory for anything touching operational systems.

industries.label: Other / General Enterprise
industries.framing: Cross-industry workloads where the economics of owning inference capacity stand on their own.

use_case_categories.label: Quantitative & Risk Analytics
use_case_categories.note: PROPOSED seventh category — added to house the three capital-markets blueprints that had no clean home. Drop it and refile those three if you would rather stay at six.

blueprints.name: NVIDIA RAG Blueprint
blueprints.description: Lets an organization's own documents power an AI assistant that answers from those documents, with citations, instead of guessing from general training data.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Turn the documents your people already can't find into answers they can get in seconds, with citations back to the source.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: A retrieval pipeline that indexes your existing documents and uses them to ground an AI assistant's answers. Handles text, tables, charts, and images in the same pipeline, and cites which document each answer came from. Deployable in your own environment, so the documents never leave it.

detail_in_practice.default: Point it at the document repositories your staff currently search by hand: policies, procedures, contracts, technical manuals. Staff ask questions in plain language and get sourced answers instead of a list of files to open.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Point it at municipal code, permit requirements, and benefits eligibility rules. Constituents get straight answers about zoning or licensing without a phone call, and staff stop re-answering the same twenty questions.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Point it at clinical protocols, formulary, payer policy, and credentialing documentation. Clinical and administrative staff get sourced answers without paging through binders or portals mid-shift.
detail_in_practice.legal: Point it at your matter files, precedent library, and contract archive. Associates get cited answers from your own work product rather than starting research from zero, and privileged material stays inside your walls.
detail_in_practice.food-cpg: Point it at HACCP plans, supplier certifications, and food safety records. Plant and QA staff get audit-ready answers on the floor instead of walking back to a filing cabinet.
detail_in_practice.education: Point it at the student handbook, financial aid policy, and course catalog. Students and families self-serve the routine questions that currently consume the front office.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Mid-size open model plus an embedding model. Small pilots run on a single node; production scales with concurrent users more than document volume.

blueprints.name: NVIDIA AI-Q Blueprint for Intelligent Agents
blueprints.description: A research agent that plans a line of inquiry, pulls from multiple sources, and writes a cited report rather than a one-line answer.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Hand off the research that eats an analyst's week and get back a cited report you can actually check.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: An agent that classifies what you're asking, decides how deep to go, runs multiple researchers in parallel across your sources, and produces a citation-backed report. You can ask follow-up questions against a finished report or re-run it with new inputs.

detail_in_practice.default: Give it the research task a subject matter expert would otherwise spend days on, pulling across internal archives and approved external sources, and review the cited draft instead of building it from scratch.
detail_in_practice.legal: Case law synthesis and discovery support where every assertion needs a citation. The blueprint's source-citation design lines up with how legal work already gets checked.
detail_in_practice.federal-defense: Capture and proposal research across past performance libraries, solicitations, and technical archives, inside your own boundary.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Rate case preparation and regulatory filing research across dockets, precedent, and internal operational data.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Prior authorization research, coverage determination, and literature synthesis with sources attached.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Larger reasoning model plus retrieval components. Agentic workloads burn more tokens per task than chat, which is exactly the pattern where owned capacity beats metered API pricing.

blueprints.name: Video Search and Summarization (VSS)
blueprints.description: Makes video searchable in plain language, so you can ask what happened on camera instead of scrubbing footage.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Stop scrubbing footage. Ask what happened, get the clip, and get an alert next time it happens.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Vision language models watch your video, summarize what's in it, answer questions about it, and raise alerts on conditions you define. Works on live feeds and archives. Note this is review, search, and alerting rather than a high-speed per-frame inspection system.

detail_in_practice.default: Point it at cameras you already have. Instead of assigning someone to watch or scrub, ask what happened during a window and get the clips plus a summary.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Facility safety, fall risk in common areas, OR utilization review, and entrance security. Keep the framing on operational and safety review rather than anything patient-monitoring-adjacent.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Remote site monitoring, flare stack observation, right-of-way surveillance, and PPE compliance in hazardous areas, at sites where nobody is watching a monitor.
detail_in_practice.retail-distribution: Loss prevention, queue and staffing analysis, and safety compliance across stores without adding headcount to watch feeds.
detail_in_practice.transportation-logistics: Yard and terminal monitoring, equipment inspection review, and incident investigation across a distributed asset base.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Public safety camera review, traffic incident analysis, and facility security. Worth pairing with a clear retention and access policy, since this is the use case constituents ask about.
detail_in_practice.general-manufacturing: Line monitoring, quality review, and worker safety compliance, with searchable history when something goes wrong.
detail_in_practice.legal: Deposition and hearing video review, plus searchable video evidence in discovery, where review volume is growing faster than anyone's capacity to watch it.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Vision language models are the heaviest inference profile in the catalog and scale with concurrent camera streams. This is the use case most likely to justify dedicated on-premises capacity on cost alone.

blueprints.name: Streaming Data to RAG
blueprints.description: Turns live sensor and signal data into something you can ask questions about, instead of only charting it on a dashboard.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Make the sensor data you already collect answerable in plain language, not just plottable.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Ingests streaming sensor and signal data, indexes it continuously, and lets operators query it conversationally alongside their reference documentation. The result is situational awareness you can interrogate rather than a wall of gauges.

detail_in_practice.default: Feed it the telemetry you already collect and let operators ask what changed, when, and what the procedure says to do about it.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: SCADA, substation, and smart meter telemetry made queryable alongside operating procedures, so an operator can ask what changed on a feeder and what the procedure says next.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Wellhead, pipeline, and processing telemetry from sites with intermittent connectivity, processed at the edge where it's generated.
detail_in_practice.transportation-logistics: Telematics from vehicles, rail cars, and containers, queryable by corridor, asset, or time window.
detail_in_practice.general-manufacturing: Equipment telemetry from the line, indexed against maintenance history and manuals so anomalies come with context.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Continuous ingest plus retrieval. Edge-deployable, which matters most where connectivity is the constraint rather than cost.

blueprints.name: NVIDIA Data Flywheel Blueprint
blueprints.description: A loop that keeps retraining and re-evaluating your models on your own usage data, so smaller and cheaper models can take over work the big ones started.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Your AI gets cheaper and better the longer you run it, because it learns from your traffic instead of staying frozen.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: An automated cycle that captures production traffic, evaluates whether a smaller model could handle it at target accuracy, and promotes the cheaper model when it can. Over time the expensive model handles less of the volume.

detail_in_practice.default: Run it behind whatever you deploy first. Month one you're paying for a large model on every request; month six a distilled model is handling the routine traffic at a fraction of the compute, on hardware you already own.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Needs training capacity alongside inference, which is the clearest argument in the catalog for owning rather than renting: this workload only pays off if the hardware is already yours.

blueprints.name: Nemotron Voice Agent
blueprints.description: A real-time voice assistant that listens, understands, and speaks back, built to run on your own infrastructure.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Answer the routine calls that never stop coming, in natural voice, without adding headcount.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: End-to-end voice agent combining speech recognition, a language model, and speech synthesis with low enough latency for real conversation. Handles inquiry, lookup, and handoff to a human when it should.

detail_in_practice.default: Put it on the line that generates the most repetitive calls. It handles the routine ninety percent and hands the rest to staff with context already gathered.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Outage reporting and billing inquiry, where call volume spikes hardest exactly when staff are least available.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: 311 and service request lines, reaching constituents who will call but won't use a web form.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Hands-free field operations support for crews who are gloved, at height, or otherwise unable to use a screen.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Latency-sensitive: speech in, model, speech out, all under conversational thresholds. This is the workload where local inference most visibly beats a cloud round trip.

blueprints.name: PDF to Podcast
blueprints.description: Converts documents into a natural-sounding audio discussion people can listen to instead of read.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Get the long document read by the people who need it, by letting them listen on the drive instead of promising to read it later.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Takes a document and produces a conversational audio version, summarized and structured for listening rather than read aloud verbatim.

detail_in_practice.default: Use it on the documents your people are supposed to read and don't: policy updates, safety bulletins, procedure changes.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Council agendas, budget documents, and policy proposals as audio, which doubles as a civic transparency story and demos extremely well.
detail_in_practice.transportation-logistics: Safety bulletins and procedure updates for drivers and crews who are effectively never at a desk.
detail_in_practice.education: Handbooks, syllabi, and policy documents in audio, which carries a real accessibility benefit alongside the convenience.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Batch workload, latency-tolerant. Cheap to run alongside heavier tools on the same hardware.

blueprints.name: Content Localization
blueprints.description: Translates and localizes media, including syncing speakers' lips to the translated audio.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Reach the part of your audience you're currently only serving in one language, without rebuilding the content.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Translates media content, generates localized audio, and synchronizes speaker lip movement to the new audio track across multiple speakers.

detail_in_practice.default: Run existing training, safety, and communication content through it to produce versions in the languages your audience actually speaks.
detail_in_practice.education: Course materials and family communications in a district's home languages, which is often both an equity commitment and a compliance obligation.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Constituent communications in required languages, produced in-house rather than through a translation vendor cycle.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Safety and training content for a globally distributed workforce, where comprehension is a safety issue rather than a convenience.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Batch multimodal workload combining translation, speech synthesis, and video generation. Heavier than text but fully latency-tolerant.

blueprints.name: GPU Query Engine (GQE)
blueprints.description: A GPU-accelerated SQL engine that runs large analytical queries dramatically faster than CPU-based warehouses.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Run the queries your team currently schedules overnight in the time it takes to get coffee.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: A reference architecture for GPU-accelerated SQL processing, letting existing analytical workloads run on GPU hardware instead of scaling out CPU clusters.

detail_in_practice.default: Aim it at the analytical workloads that are currently slow enough that people avoid asking questions: multi-year operational history, cross-system joins, large aggregations.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Seismic, production, and reservoir datasets, which are among the largest structured data volumes in any industry.
detail_in_practice.legal: E-discovery processing across large document productions, where turnaround time is a cost driver.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Data-processing rather than inference, so it sizes on data volume and query concurrency rather than model size. Often shares a cluster with inference workloads.

blueprints.name: LLM Router
blueprints.description: Routes each request to the most appropriate model, so simple questions don't consume expensive capacity.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Stop paying premium-model prices for questions a small model could have answered.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Classifies incoming requests and dispatches them to the best-fit model for the task, balancing quality against cost and latency. Also produces a record of which model handled what.

detail_in_practice.default: Deploy it in front of a mixed model fleet. Routine lookups go to a small fast model, hard reasoning goes to a large one, and you get an audit trail of the split.
detail_in_practice.financial-services: The routing log doubles as model governance evidence, which matters when a regulator asks which system produced a given output.
detail_in_practice.legal: Useful where AI-assisted work is billed to clients and the firm needs a defensible record of what handled which matter.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Lightweight itself, but it presumes you're running several models, which is a fleet-scale argument rather than a single-node one.

blueprints.name: NemoClaw Governed Agent Suite
blueprints.description: Three related blueprints for running autonomous coding and workflow agents inside enterprise guardrails and sandboxing.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Give developers real autonomous agents without giving them ungoverned access to your systems.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Covers NemoClaw for LangChain Deep Agents Code, for Hermes Agent, and for OpenClaw. All three run agents that plan, edit, and test work autonomously, with sandboxing and enterprise governance around what the agent can reach.

detail_in_practice.default: Stand it up where developer productivity matters but ungoverned agent access is a non-starter. The governance layer is the reason this is deployable in environments that would otherwise ban agentic tools outright.
detail_in_practice.federal-defense: The sandboxing story is what makes agentic development viable inside an accreditation boundary.
detail_in_practice.legal: Client confidentiality and privilege make ungoverned agent access untenable; the guardrails are the point.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: NERC CIP obligations around critical infrastructure make governed agent execution a requirement rather than a preference.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Long-running agent sessions consume far more tokens than interactive chat, making sustained throughput the sizing driver.
blueprints.internal_note: Bundled as one card to avoid three near-identical entries. Split if customers start asking for a specific variant.

blueprints.name: Nsight Copilot
blueprints.description: A coding assistant specialized in CUDA and GPU programming, grounded in authoritative GPU development documentation.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Give your HPC and simulation engineers an assistant that actually knows GPU programming.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: An AI coding assistant with CUDA-aware chat, real-time completion, and retrieval grounded in GPU programming documentation. Runs on DGX Spark class hardware.

detail_in_practice.default: For teams writing or porting GPU code. Narrow audience, but high value where it applies.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Reservoir simulation and computational engineering teams already running serious HPC.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Grid modeling and power systems simulation groups.
detail_in_practice.financial-services: Quantitative research and risk compute teams.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Workstation or single-node class. Runs on DGX Spark, so it's a low barrier to entry compared with the rest of the catalog.

blueprints.name: Financial Fraud Detection
blueprints.description: Detects fraud by modeling the relationships between accounts and transactions, not just individual transaction features.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Catch the fraud rings that per-transaction rules miss, because the pattern is in the connections.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Uses graph neural networks to spot fraudulent patterns across networks of accounts and transactions, catching coordinated activity that transaction-level rules score as individually normal.

detail_in_practice.default: Point it at transaction and claim data where you suspect organized rather than opportunistic fraud.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Claims fraud, where coordinated billing patterns across providers are exactly the graph problem this solves.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Benefits, procurement, and tax fraud, with a direct revenue-recovery argument for a budget-constrained agency.
detail_in_practice.federal-defense: Improper payments and procurement fraud, a standing federal priority with real dollar recovery attached.
detail_in_practice.transportation-logistics: Cargo theft and fictitious pickup schemes, a live and growing problem in freight.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Energy theft and billing fraud detection across meter and account networks.
detail_in_practice.education: Financial aid and enrollment fraud, which has grown sharply with online enrollment.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Graph model training plus real-time scoring. Training is periodic and heavy; inference is light and latency-sensitive.

blueprints.name: Build Your Own Transaction Foundation Model
blueprints.description: Trains a foundation model on your own tabular transaction history, producing embeddings that feed fraud, risk, and personalization systems.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Build a model that understands your customers' sequences of behavior, not just their last transaction.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Applies transformer architecture to tabular transaction data to produce embeddings that capture behavioral sequence, then feeds those embeddings into downstream fraud, risk, and personalization models.

detail_in_practice.default: Use where sequences of events carry more signal than any single event: what happened before this, and how unusual is that pattern for this account.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Meter reading and billing sequences, for both theft detection and consumption forecasting.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Claims sequences, where the order and timing of events carries the signal.
detail_in_practice.retail-distribution: Customer behavior modeling for personalization as well as return and payment fraud.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Genuine training workload on your own proprietary data, which cannot be outsourced to an API. Sizes on data volume and training cadence.

blueprints.name: Quantitative Portfolio Optimization
blueprints.description: Runs portfolio optimization fast enough to be used in real time rather than as an overnight batch.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Optimize the portfolio while the market is still moving, not after it closed.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: GPU-accelerated portfolio optimization using cuOpt, built for institutional scale and real-time rebalancing.

detail_in_practice.default: For asset managers and institutional desks where optimization runtime currently dictates how often the portfolio can be rebalanced.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Optimization rather than inference. Sizes on portfolio complexity and rebalancing frequency.

blueprints.name: Quantitative Signal Discovery Agent
blueprints.description: Automates the discovery, testing, and refinement of trading signals for quantitative research teams.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Test more hypotheses than your quant team could work through by hand, and keep the ones that survive.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: An agentic workflow that proposes candidate trading signals, backtests them, and refines the survivors, scaling the throughput of a quantitative research process.

detail_in_practice.default: For quant desks where the bottleneck is analyst time spent formulating and testing hypotheses rather than access to data.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Agentic plus heavy backtesting compute. Sustained rather than bursty.

blueprints.name: AI Model Distillation for Financial Data
blueprints.description: Distills large models down to smaller domain-specific ones for financial data, cutting the cost of running signals at scale.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Run market signal generation at production scale without paying frontier-model prices per call.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Applies the Data Flywheel pattern to unstructured financial data, distilling domain-specific models that generate market signals at a fraction of the compute cost of the model that trained them.

detail_in_practice.default: For firms already running signal generation at volume where per-call model cost has become the limiting factor on how much can be processed.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Training plus inference on the same footprint, the classic own-don't-rent profile.

blueprints.name: Retail Shopping Assistant
blueprints.description: A multi-agent shopping advisor with image search and cart management, for online and in-store use.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Give every shopper the attention of your best associate, including the ones shopping at 2am.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Multi-agent architecture handling product discovery, image-based search, recommendation, and cart management, with streaming responses.

detail_in_practice.default: Deploy across web, app, and in-store kiosk so the same assistant handles discovery wherever the customer is.
detail_in_practice.general-manufacturing: The same mechanic works as a B2B parts configurator, where selecting the right component from a deep catalog is the actual customer problem.
detail_in_practice.food-cpg: For brands going direct-to-consumer, where you own the storefront but not decades of retail merchandising experience.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Multi-agent plus vision plus retrieval, with consumer-facing latency requirements and traffic that spikes seasonally.

blueprints.name: Retail Agentic Commerce
blueprints.description: Reference implementation of emerging agentic commerce protocols, enabling AI-driven checkout while you stay merchant of record.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Be ready when your customers' AI agents start doing the buying, instead of being disintermediated by them.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Implements the Agentic Commerce Protocol and Universal Commerce Protocol so AI agents can negotiate and complete checkout against your storefront while you remain merchant of record.

detail_in_practice.default: This is a positioning conversation as much as a deployment one: agent-driven purchasing is arriving, and the question is whether your storefront can transact with an agent or only with a human.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Protocol and integration heavy rather than compute heavy. The strategic weight outsizes the infrastructure footprint.

blueprints.name: Retail Catalog Enrichment
blueprints.description: Turns basic product images and data into rich, localized catalog content automatically.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Fill in the catalog content nobody has time to write, from the product images you already have.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Vision language models read product imagery and generate descriptions, attributes, and localized copy, replacing a heavily manual content production process.

detail_in_practice.default: Aim it at the catalog backlog: items with a photo, a SKU, and nothing else.
detail_in_practice.general-manufacturing: Parts and equipment catalogs, where incomplete data is a genuine sales and service friction point.
detail_in_practice.food-cpg: Product content fed downstream to retail partners, which is a constant and constantly manual obligation.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Supply and equipment catalogs across a large system's purchasing operation.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Batch vision and generation. Latency-tolerant, so it fills idle capacity on hardware bought for something else.

blueprints.name: Multi-Agent Intelligent Warehouse
blueprints.description: A multi-agent system for warehouse operations, combining automation, real-time monitoring, and plain-language interaction.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Ask your warehouse what's happening instead of waiting for the report that says what happened.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Coordinated agents monitor warehouse operations, optimize task allocation, and answer operational questions conversationally.

detail_in_practice.default: For any operation where inventory and throughput questions currently require someone to pull a report or walk the floor.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Central supply and sterile processing, where stockouts have clinical consequences.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Storm materials staging and transformer inventory, where readiness is the whole point.
detail_in_practice.federal-defense: Depot and sustainment inventory across distributed sites.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Remote site parts staging, where a missing component means a crew waits days.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Multi-agent orchestration plus continuous monitoring ingest. Site-level deployment fits the edge pattern.

blueprints.name: Ambient Healthcare Agents
blueprints.description: Voice-driven agents that capture and structure the conversation in the room, so the documentation writes itself.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Give your people back the hours they spend documenting what they just did.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Combines speech recognition, language models, and speech synthesis into agents that support both providers and patients, including ambient capture of an encounter into structured documentation.

detail_in_practice.default: Deploy where a professional's day splits between the work and writing up the work.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Ambient clinical documentation, currently the highest-demand AI use case in health systems, plus patient-facing agents for intake and follow-up.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Social services caseworkers and public health staff carry a nearly identical documentation burden, and this is an angle most agencies haven't considered.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Real-time speech plus language modeling, and in healthcare the PHI constraint makes local inference close to a requirement rather than a preference.

blueprints.name: Biomedical AI-Q Research Agent
blueprints.description: The AI-Q research agent specialized for biomedical literature and data.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Compress a literature review from weeks to an afternoon, with citations intact.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Applies the AI-Q research agent pattern to biomedical corpora, producing cited synthesis across literature and research data.

detail_in_practice.default: For research teams whose bottleneck is reading and synthesizing prior work rather than generating new data.
detail_in_practice.education: Research universities and academic medical centers, a natural fit for the higher-ed side of this vertical.
detail_in_practice.food-cpg: Food science and ag-biotech research groups working the same literature-heavy problem.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Same profile as AI-Q with domain-specific retrieval. Research institutions often already own GPU capacity this can share.

blueprints.name: Single Cell Analysis
blueprints.description: Accelerates single-cell data analysis from days to minutes using GPU-accelerated data science libraries.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Turn an overnight analysis run into a coffee break, so researchers iterate instead of waiting.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: GPU-accelerated single-cell analysis via RAPIDS-singlecell, compressing standard research workflows from days to minutes.

detail_in_practice.default: For labs where analysis turnaround dictates how many hypotheses get tested in a grant cycle.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Data-science acceleration rather than inference. Sizes on dataset scale.

blueprints.name: Genomics Analysis
blueprints.description: GPU-accelerated genomic sequencing and analysis pipelines.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Cut sequencing analysis time enough that genomics becomes a clinical tool, not just a research one.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Accelerates genomic sequencing analysis pipelines on GPU infrastructure.

detail_in_practice.default: For sequencing operations where pipeline runtime is the constraint on throughput or clinical turnaround.
detail_in_practice.federal-defense: National labs and biodefense programs running sequencing at scale.
detail_in_practice.food-cpg: Ag-biotech and food safety genomics, including pathogen tracing.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Pipeline acceleration sized on sequencing volume. Sustained utilization makes owned hardware straightforward to justify.

blueprints.name: NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint for AI Factory Digital Twins
blueprints.description: Design, simulate, and operate AI factory infrastructure as a digital twin before and after it is built.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Design the facility, the power, and the cooling together as a simulation before you pour concrete.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Unites facility design, hardware layout, power, and cooling into a single simulated model, validated against a real build. Aimed specifically at AI factory infrastructure rather than general facility twins.

detail_in_practice.default: Most relevant when you're standing up AI infrastructure of your own rather than modeling an existing production process. Worth setting that expectation early so it isn't mistaken for a general-purpose plant twin.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Utilities are unusually well positioned here, owning both the power and the land, and several are actively evaluating AI infrastructure as a business.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Relevant where a jurisdiction is pursuing sovereign AI capacity rather than renting it.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Omniverse simulation workloads plus the AI factory being designed. This one is upstream of the infrastructure conversation rather than downstream of it.

blueprints.name: Cosmos Dataset Search
blueprints.description: Vector search and retrieval across very large video datasets, built for training autonomous systems.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Find the handful of edge cases hiding in a petabyte of video, instead of training on whatever you happened to label.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Semantic search and retrieval over large video datasets, so teams training perception models can find specific scenarios rather than sampling blindly.

detail_in_practice.default: For anyone training vision models on their own footage where the hard part is curating the training set, not running the training.
detail_in_practice.transportation-logistics: Autonomous vehicle and yard automation development.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Drone-based transmission and distribution inspection programs.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Surgical robotics and procedural video research.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Embedding generation across large video corpora plus vector search at scale. Storage-heavy alongside GPU-heavy.

blueprints.name: 3D Object Generation
blueprints.description: Generates 3D objects and assets from prompts or references, for design and simulation pipelines.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Populate a simulation or a product visualization without modeling every asset by hand.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Generates 3D assets programmatically for use in design, visualization, and simulation environments.

detail_in_practice.default: Useful wherever asset creation is the bottleneck in a visualization or simulation effort.
detail_in_practice.state-local-gov: Urban planning visualization and capital project modeling for public presentation.
detail_in_practice.retail-distribution: Product visualization and virtual showroom assets.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Generative workload, batch-friendly, often workstation-class for smaller teams.

blueprints.name: 3D-Guided Generative AI (RTX)
blueprints.description: Controls AI image generation using a rough 3D scene, so you get the composition you intended rather than what the prompt happened to produce.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Get marketing and design imagery with the composition you actually wanted, on a workstation rather than a cluster.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: Combines a 3D scene tool with image generation so the layout of the scene controls the composition of the generated image. Runs on RTX workstations.

detail_in_practice.default: For design and marketing teams producing visual content at volume, where prompt-only generation wastes time on composition retries.
detail_in_practice.retail-distribution: Product and campaign imagery produced in-house rather than through a photo shoot cycle.
detail_in_practice.food-cpg: Packaging and marketing visuals across many SKUs and markets.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: RTX workstation class. The lowest infrastructure barrier in the catalog, which makes it a useful low-risk first deployment.

blueprints.name: AI Agent for Telecom Network Configuration Planning
blueprints.description: Uses agentic AI to plan and optimize radio network configuration parameters.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Tune the network you own without a specialist manually working through parameter combinations.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: An agentic framework that plans and optimizes radio access network parameters using simulation and language-model-driven reasoning.

detail_in_practice.default: Relevant to any organization operating its own wireless infrastructure rather than buying connectivity as a service.
detail_in_practice.general-manufacturing: Private 5G on plant floors, an area growing fast and short on in-house RF expertise.
detail_in_practice.healthcare: Hospital wireless environments where coverage gaps have clinical consequences.
detail_in_practice.oil-gas: Remote site communications where connectivity is the operating constraint.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Simulation plus agentic reasoning, run periodically rather than continuously.

blueprints.name: AI Virtual Assistant for Customer Service
blueprints.description: A text-based customer service assistant grounded in your own knowledge base.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Handle the routine inquiries in text, grounded in your own documentation.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: A reference text-based virtual assistant integrating a knowledge base with customer service workflows.

detail_in_practice.default: Deprecated by NVIDIA as of April 2026 and retained for reference only. The RAG Blueprint is the current path for this use case; keep this entry visible only if you want the historical mapping.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Superseded. Size against the RAG Blueprint instead.

blueprints.name: AI Weather Analytics with Earth-2
blueprints.description: AI-driven weather analysis and forecasting with multi-layered geospatial visualization.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Forecast the weather that drives your load, your routes, or your outages at your own resolution.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: AI weather prediction and geospatial analytics built on Earth-2.

detail_in_practice.default: Marked deprecated on NVIDIA's catalog. Worth keeping visible because the underlying use case is core to several industries and NVIDIA may well reintroduce it.
detail_in_practice.utilities-energy: Weather-driven load forecasting and storm response planning, arguably more central to utilities than to any other industry.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Forecasting model inference on geospatial data. Deprecated status means treat as directional until NVIDIA clarifies a successor.

blueprints.name: Bring Your Own LLM to NIM
blueprints.description: Packages a model you already chose or fine-tuned into NVIDIA's optimized serving format.
blueprints.industry_pitch: Run the model you picked, on your hardware, with the serving performance you paid for.
blueprints.detail_what_it_does: A path for taking an open or fine-tuned model and deploying it as an optimized NIM microservice on your own infrastructure.

detail_in_practice.default: The connective tissue between choosing a model and running it well. Pairs directly with the Open-Weight Model Advisor: that tool picks the model, this deploys it.

blueprints.detail_infrastructure: Serving optimization rather than a use case in itself. Sizing comes from the model chosen.
